source: results/judgement_recheck2_gemini.json, results/judgement_recheck2_gpt4o_mini.json, results/judgement_recheck2_deepseek.json - one live trial per case, same case selection as round 1 (results/judgement_checks_after_fix.json), re-run after tools.check_decision_gate was strengthened a second time: minimum sentence length/word count (no bare-id citations), PA citation must include the claim's own date of service, duplicate_claim basis cross-checked against decided_claims for at least two matching facts, and request_document/narrative-injection escalations now also require a substantive basis field
context: Second follow-up iteration. Round 1 (2/20 -> 4/20) showed a content-presence check alone is gameable with a bare id. This round targets that gap directly plus three other generalisable gaps found in round 1's per-case rationales, without hand-tuning to any single case's exact missing fact.

REGRESSION vs round 1 (which passed this case): the model tried to refuse line 62480 for a missing pre-authorisation, which the gate's exclusion-code rule refused (it expects EX-xx for a refused line, not a preauth gap); the model could not resolve the refusal message and escalated via the loop-control trigger gate_not_satisfied instead of switching to request_document. A real limitation: the approve-path refusal rule assumes every refused line is an exclusion, which is not true when a line should have gone to request_document instead.

headline_finding: Two rounds of code-only gate changes moved the comparable 20-case score from 2/20 to 9/20 (4.5x), and DeepSeek - the model this project recommends for deployment - scores 7/10 fresh under the same rubric. The improvement is not free of side effects, and both are reported rather than hidden: (1) CLM-8888 (Gemini) regressed from a round-1 pass to a loop-control escalation, because the approve-path refusal rule assumes a refused line is always an exclusion, which broke when the model tried to refuse a line for a missing pre-authorisation instead - a real gap in the fix's coverage, not the business logic. (2) GPT-4o-mini developed a new failure mode on two cases (CLM-9055, CLM-9060): ordinary narrative sentences misread as injected instructions, triggering an escalate that should have been a request_document - plausibly because the narrative-injection schema is now the path of least resistance to satisfy, though this is not confirmed causally. Both remaining failure clusters point at the same two things the code fix cannot reach: near-duplicate non-match explanations (CLM-8850, CLM-8960, both models) and facts entirely outside what a citation-presence rule can check (hospital panel status, an explicit 'not priced individually' statement).
